harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1: created group inventory-readers and user inventorysvc, then set ownership to inventorysvc:inventory-readers with 750 on directories and 640 on files, preserving all existing data. Verified access control by testing with a group-member user (read succeeded) and an unrelated user (permission denied), then cleaned up the test accounts. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured a boot_id/data-checksum baseline, issued a native `reboot`, polled through the outage, confirmed a changed boot_id after recovery, and re-verified ownership, permissions, and identical data checksums post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory contents, ownership, and existing users/groups on node1
Created group inventory-readers and user inventorysvc (nologin) via addgroup/adduser
chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers /srv/inventory
chmod 750 on all directories, chmod 640 on all files under /srv/inventory
Verified read access for a inventory-readers group member and denied access for an unrelated user, then deleted both test accounts
Captured pre-restart boot_id and data checksums as baseline
Triggered native `reboot` on node1 with the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified ownership, permissions, and data checksums matched baseline after restart

evidence.requirement: Existing data preserved with correct ownership (inventorysvc) and permissions (readable by inventory-readers, inaccessible to others)
evidence.summary: Initial state showed root-owned data with no inventorysvc/inventory-readers. Created the group/user, then chowned to inventorysvc:inventory-readers and set 750/640 perms while file contents were left untouched.

evidence.requirement: Access control functions as required (readers can read, others cannot)
evidence.summary: Test user in inventory-readers successfully read records.csv; unrelated test user got Permission denied on both ls and cat. Both test accounts were then fully removed (confirmed via getent).

evidence.requirement: Data contents preserved (unmodified) through the repair
evidence.summary: records.csv and config.json contents/checksums were captured before restart and matched exactly after restart, confirming no data was altered.
Captured baseline boot_id (e8db0482-...) and md5 checksums of the inventory data plus directory listing showing correct ownership/permissions prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: restart acknowledged and executed
evidence.summary: Issued a backgrounded `reboot` so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect; the subsequent poll showed connection reset, confirming the node went down.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity proven
evidence.summary: After polling through the outage, exec access returned with a new boot_id (bcbaec9f-...), differing from the pre-restart boot_id (e8db0482-...), proving an actual OS restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: post-restart recovery of required data/service state
evidence.summary: Post-restart check confirmed /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers), permissions (750/640), and data checksums matched the pre-restart baseline exactly, and both the inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group still exist.
